source_text:
Οὐ γὰρ εἴσω τῶν σωματικῶν ὄγκων ἡ ἀνωτάτω Σοφία καθειργμένη περιέχεται, καθάπερ αἱ τῶν ὑγρῶν καὶ ξηρῶν ὕλαι τῶν μὲν ἀγγείων εἴσω
κατακλείονται, περιέχονται δὲ μᾶλλον ἢ περιέχουσι τὰς θήκας. Ἀλλὰ θεία τις οὖσα καὶ ἀνέκφραστος δύναμις, τὰ δ' ἐνδοτάτω καὶ ἐξωτάτω τοῦ νεὼ περιλαμβάνουσα κραταιοῖ, κἀντεῦθεν ἐπέκεινα διήκουσα, πάντας ὁμοῦ τοὺς ὄγκους κρατεῖ περιέχουσα. 31 Εἰ δ' ὁ ἥλιος, σῶμα ὢν ὁρατὸν, καὶ αἰσθήσει καταληπτὸν, τοσαύτας καὶ τοιαύτας πανταχοῦ γῆς ὑπομένων αἰκίας, οὐ μεταβάλλει τὴν τάξιν, οὐδὲ αἴσθηται μικρᾶς ἢ μεγάλης πληγῆς, τὴν ἀσώματον Σοφίαν οἰόμεθα χραίνεσθαι, καὶ μεταλλάττειν τὴν φύσιν, εἰ ὁ ναὸς αὐτῆς σταυρῷ προσηλοῦται, ἢ λύσιν ὑπομένει, ἢ τρῶσιν ὑφίσταται, ἢ διαφθορὰν δέχεται; Ἀλλὰ πάσχει μὲν ὁ νεὼς, ἡ δὲ ἀκηλίδωτος οὐσία παντάπασιν ἄχραντος τὴν ἀξίαν καθέστηκεν. 32 Βαδιοῦμαι δὲ ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ πεπραγμένα. Τί οὖν; ἐπειδὴ διὰ ταῦτα σύνοδος εἰς τὴν Νικαέων ἀφικνεῖται μεγίστη, διακοσίων μήτι γε καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα τὸν ἀριθμὸν ὁμόσε συναχθέντων (τὸ γὰρ σαφὲς διὰ τὸν τῆς πολυανδρίας ὄχλον οὐκ οἷός τέ εἰμι γράφειν, ἐπειδὴ μὴ πάντη τοῦτο περισπουδάστως ἀνίχνευον), ὡς δὲ ἐζητεῖτο τῆς πίστεως ὁ τρόπος, ἐναργὴς μὲν ἔλεγχος τὸ γράμμα τῆς Εὐσεβίου προὐβάλλετο βλασφημίας. Ἐπὶ πάντων δὲ ἀναγνωσθὲν, αὐτίκα συμφορὰν μὲν ἀστάθμητον τῆς ἐκτροπῆς ἕνεκα τοῖς αὐτηκόοις προὐξένει, αἰσχύνην δὲ ἀνήκεστον τῷ γράψαντι παρεῖχεν. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ τὸ ἐργαστήριον τῶν ἀμφὶ τὸν Εὐσέβιον σαφῶς ἑάλω, τοῦ παρανόμου γράμματος διαρραγέντος ὑπ' ὄψει πάντων ὁμοῦ τινες ἐκ συσκευῆς, τοὔνομα προβαλλόμενοι τῆς εἰρήνης, κατεσίγησαν μὲν ἅπαντας τοὺς ἄριστα λέγειν εἰωθότας. Οἱ δ' Ἀρειομανῖται δείσαντες μή πη ἄρα τοσαύτης ἐν ταὐτῷ συνόδου συγκεκροτημένης ἐξοστρακισθεῖεν, ἀναθεματίζουσι μὲν προπηδήσαντες τὸ ἀπηγορευμένον δόγμα, συμφώνοις γράμμασιν ὑπογράψαντες αὐτοχειρί. Τῶν δὲ προεδριῶν διὰ πλείστης ὅσης περιδρομῆς κρατήσαντες, δέον αὐτοὺς ὑπόπτωσιν λαμβάνειν, τότε μὲν λεληθότως, τότε δὲ προφανῶς τὰς ἀποψηφισθείσας πρεσβεύουσι δόξας, διαφόροις ἐπιβουλεύοντες τοῖς ἐλέγχοις. Βουλόμενοι δὲ δὴ παγιῶσαι τὰ ζιζανιώδη φυτουργήματα, δεδοίκασι τοὺς ἐφόρους· καὶ ταύτῃ τοὺς τῆς εὐσεβείας κήρυκας ἐκπολέμουσιν. Οὐχ οὕτως δὲ πιστεύομεν, ὡς ἀνθρώπους ἀθέους δύνασθαι κρατῆσαι πώποτε τοῦ θείου. Κἂν γὰρ πάλιν ἰσχύσωσι, πάλιν ἡττηθήσονται κατὰ τὸν σεμνόφωνον προφήτην Ἡσαΐαν.
thought_title: The impassible Wisdom and the exposure of Eusebius at Nicaea
orientation: Eustathius is closing his treatise by arguing that the divine Wisdom cannot be defiled by the crucifixion of its temple, then recounting how Eusebius's written statement was exposed as blasphemy at the Council of Nicaea.
pass_a_gloss: For the highest Wisdom is not imprisoned and contained within bodily masses, just as the materials of wet and dry things are shut up inside vessels, and are contained rather than contain their receptacles. But being a certain divine and inexpressible power, and encompassing the innermost and outermost parts of the temple, it strengthens it, and extending from there beyond, it holds all masses together, containing them. If the sun, being a visible body and perceptible to sense, enduring so many and such outrages everywhere on earth, does not change its order, nor perceives a small or great blow, do we think the incorporeal Wisdom is defiled, and changes its nature, if its temple is nailed to a cross, or undergoes dissolution, or sustains a wound, or receives corruption? But the temple suffers, while the undefiled substance has remained altogether unstained in its dignity. I will proceed from here now also to the things that were done. What then? Since on account of these things a very great council arrives at the city of the Nicaeans, of two hundred and seventy in number gathered together (for I am not able to write the exact number because of the crowd of the multitude, since I did not trace this out with complete diligence), as the manner of the faith was being sought, the written statement of Eusebius was put forward as a clear proof of blasphemy. And when it was read before all, immediately it procured an immeasurable calamity for the hearers on account of the deviation, and provided unhealable shame for the writer. And when the workshop of those around Eusebius was clearly convicted, the lawless document having been torn up before the eyes of all, certain ones together by conspiracy, putting forward the name of peace, silenced all those accustomed to speak best. And the Arians, fearing lest they be banished when so great a council had been convened in the same place, anathematize, leaping forward, the condemned doctrine, having subscribed with their own hand in agreed writings. And having seized the presiding seats through very great maneuvering, when they ought to receive humiliation, at one time secretly, at another time openly they promote the condemned opinions, plotting against the refutations with various schemes. And wishing to make firm the tares-like plantings, they fear the overseers; and in this way they make war on the heralds of piety. But we do not believe thus, that godless men can ever prevail over the divine. For even if they grow strong again, again they will be defeated according to the august-voiced prophet Isaiah.

choices.why: Glossary requires Wisdom for Σοφία; ἀνωτάτω is superlative, rendered 'highest' to keep the spatial metaphor of the passage.
Glossary mandates temple for ναός; here it is the human body of Christ.
ἀκηλίδωτος means spotless or undefiled; οὐσία is substance, keeping the philosophical register of the argument.
γράμμα is a written document; 'written statement' captures the official character of what was read at the council.
ζιζάνιον is the tare or weed from the parable; φυτούργημα is a cultivated planting, so 'tares-like plantings' preserves the agricultural metaphor.
σεμνόφωνος means of august or solemn voice; the compound is kept as an adjective to preserve the epithet.

pass_b_english: The highest Wisdom is not shut up and contained inside bodily masses, the way wet and dry materials are locked inside vessels and are contained by their containers rather than containing them. Instead, Wisdom is a divine and inexpressible power. It encompasses and strengthens both the innermost and outermost parts of the temple, and extending beyond from there, it holds all masses together at once by containing them.

If the sun, which is a visible body and perceptible to the senses, endures so many and such great assaults everywhere on earth without changing its order or feeling a small or great blow, do we suppose that the incorporeal Wisdom is defiled and changes its nature if its temple is nailed to a cross, or undergoes dissolution, or sustains a wound, or receives corruption? No: the temple suffers, but the undefiled substance remains altogether unstained in its dignity.

From here I will now proceed to what was done. What then? Since a very great council assembled at Nicaea for these reasons, some two hundred and seventy in number gathered together (I cannot write the exact figure because of the crowd's great size, since I did not investigate this with complete diligence), when the manner of the faith was being examined, the written statement of Eusebius was put forward as clear proof of blasphemy. When it was read before everyone, it immediately brought immeasurable disaster to those who heard it because of its deviation, and caused irreparable shame to the one who wrote it.

When the cabal of Eusebius and his party was clearly convicted, and the lawless document was torn up before the eyes of all, certain men acting by arrangement, putting forward the name of peace, silenced all those accustomed to speak most excellently. The Arians, fearing that they might be expelled from so great a council assembled in one place, leaped forward and anathematized the condemned doctrine, signing with their own hands in agreed documents. Having seized the presiding seats through the greatest possible maneuvering, when they ought to have submitted, they now secretly and now openly promote the opinions that had been voted down, plotting against those who refute them with various schemes. Wanting to make their weed-like plantings secure, they fear the officials, and in this way they make war on the heralds of piety. But we do not believe that godless men can ever prevail over the divine. For even if they grow strong again, they will be defeated again, according to the prophet Isaiah of august voice.

problems.fix: Note: Eustathius views Eusebius's theology as dangerously subordinationist.

problems.quote: they fear the imperial officials, and in this way they make war on the champions of true religion
problems.why: Logic unclear: fearing officials leads to making war? Probably means they hide behind official favor while attacking opponents.

problems.fix: 'their noxious teachings' and clarify: 'because they fear officials, they attack orthodox teachers indirectly.'

Glossary note about multiple terms for the divine nature: this is a glossary-level concern, not an error in the English text; no edit needed.
Transition 'From here I will now proceed to what was done. What then?': this follows the source's Βαδιοῦμαι δὲ ἐντεῦθεν ἤδη καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ πεπραγμένα. Τί οὖν; and is a faithful rendering; no edit needed.

'the written statement of Eusebius was put forward as clear proof of blasphemy': the source has ἐναργὴς μὲν ἔλεγχος τὸ γράμμα τῆς Εὐσεβίου προὐβάλλετο βλασφημίας, which literally means 'the written statement of Eusebius was put forward as a clear proof of blasphemy'; the English is accurate; no edit needed.

Glossary note about the incorporeal Spirit of Wisdom: this is a glossary-level concern, not an error in the English text; no edit needed.

'Weed-like plantings' and the logic of the sentence: the source has ζιζανιώδη φυτουργήματα, which means 'tares-like plantings'; the English 'weed-like plantings' is a reasonable rendering; I changed the comma to a semicolon to clarify the logical connection, but the wording is correct.
